Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 11199- 198S 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

HOPE MONOFILAMENT TWINE 

DOOR NETS 

0. I O R r W O R D 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 15 March 1985, after the draft linalized by the Textile 
Mnteriah Made from Polyolefins ( Excludintr Cordage) f^ectional 
Coinrnittee had been approved by the Textile Division ('ount il. 

0.2 These nets are mostly used in the door of the foodgrain storages of 
Food Corporation of India for preventing birds from entering the 
godowns. This standard has been prepared in collaboration with Food 
Corporation of India, New Delhi. 

0.3 I'or tiie purpose of deciding whether a parlicuhir requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS : !^-iy60*. The number ol significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the bame as that of tlie 
specified value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

!•! 'Fhis .standard prescribes the requiremems of HDPE monofilament 
twine door nets used for preventing birds from entering the grain 
storages. 

2. MANUFACTURE 
2.1 Twines 

2.1.1 The twines shall be made out of high density continuous 
monofilament polyethylene having a relative density of 0*95 to 0*96. 

2.1.2 The twine shall be of black colour (achieved by addling O'l 
percent carbon black ). These shall be flexible and consisting of 3 plies, 
each being uniform and well laid.

2.2 Border Rope 'I'iie rope used in the border of the net shall be 
made of \\\%h. density continuous monofilament polyethylene having a

2.2»1 The minimum breaking load of the rope shall be 400 N, when

2.2.2 The rope shall be of black colour ( achieved by adding 0*1 
percent carbon black ). 

2.3 Iron Riugs — Iron rings shall be ot 2*20 cm inner dia and 
chromium plated. Twenty one such iron rings shall be attached at the 
top of the net at an interval of 1!") rm and 10 rings on each side of net 
and spaced at ecpial internal. 

2.4 Iron Beads ~ Fortyone g il vanized iron beads of 50 i 5 g each shall 
be attached to the bottom border of net by HDPE twine, f) X 3 ply 
and 1 mm dia at an interval of about 7*5 cm.

3.1 The nets shall bo manufactured out of raw materials indicated 
in 2.1 to 2.4.

4. MARKING 

4,1 Each net shall be marked with the Ibllowing; 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Length and width of the piece; 

c) Manufacturers' name, initials or trade-mark, if any; and 

d) Year of manufacture. 

4.1.1 The net may also be marked with the ISI Certification mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions 
of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and 
Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian 
Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the 
requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and 
quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. 
ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions imder which a licence for tfie 
use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or proceuors, 
may be obtained from the Indian Standards Iiutitution. 

5. PACKING 

5.1 Each net shall be packed into low density polyethylene film of 60 
micron thickness or in any other suitable packing material as agreed to 
between the buyer and the seller.

6. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

6«1 Lot — The number of pieces of nets delivered to a buyer against a

6.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot, samples shall be drawn at 
random from the lot for inspection as given in Table 3. To ensure the 
randomness of selection, methods given in 18:4905-1968* may be 
followed.
